clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter's move across the country in March 1952, within the following year: June became homesick and wrote daily to her sister, Walter stayed out in the orchard and grew distant from June, Glen started fights at school, Walter cut off his brother Harlan over their father's land money, June kept to her bed for weeks that winter, Walter and June fought over money for new trees, and by September June joined the church choir and her anxiety eased. Event 113 is set aside as it has no confirmed date. These shifts pile up as the family settled into the new place, with Walter away, June anxious and then withdrawing, and Glen showing trouble at school.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failing, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard's failure in May 1968: Walter drank heavily, he and Glen blamed each other over the loan, and by October the orchard sold and the family moved to Ridgeport. Glen then took over family finances, Carl's asthma worsened that winter, and you began wetting the bed in April 1969. Walter's mother Ida's heart trouble was found in May 1969. By October Walter stopped drinking and took pruning work. The period holds within it Walter's loss of the orchard, Glen's overfunctioning response, and trouble showing in the children.

clusters.name: Glen's job lost at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job in February 1975: Glen sat out of work in the truck for months, he and Marian fought loudly over money at night, Marian took a second job cleaning offices, you stopped eating and lost weight that summer, you withdrew from your mother, Walter drank again after six years sober, and by March Glen started driving for the feed store. By June you were eating again and made the track team. Event 153 is set aside as its date is uncertain. The trouble moved from Glen's loss through the marriage and to you, settling as Glen found work.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into your house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma selling her farm and moving into your house in January 1990: you and Wilma clashed over the children's bedtimes and meals, Sam worked late and kept away from the kitchen rows, Sam took his mother's side, Owen had tantrums at preschool, Wilma took over Lily's care, you developed eczema on both hands, you and Sam fought most nights, and your mother drove over twice a week to take your side. By June 1991 Wilma took a flat in town, and your eczema cleared that summer. The shifts show you caught between Wilma and Sam, with the children reacting and you developing a symptom that lifted when Wilma left.
